title: Optically induced metallic state with persistent monoclinic symmetry in NdNiO$_3$
authors: Christian Tzschaschel, Felix Utsch, Qi Song, Spencer Doyle, Grace A. Pan, Charles M. Brooks, Julia A. Mundy, Clemens von Korff Schmising, Stefan Eisebitt
abstract: Understanding whether electronic and structural order remain coupled under nonequilibrium conditions is a central challenge in correlated materials. Here, we simultaneously track metallicity and symmetry across the photoinduced insulator-to-metal transition in NdNiO$_3$ using time-resolved optical reflectivity and symmetry-sensitive second-harmonic generation. We find that metallic reflectivity emerges at significantly lower excitation fluence than restoration of the orthorhombic high-temperature symmetry. As a result, optical excitation stabilizes a metastable state that combines the reflectivity of the metallic phase with the monoclinic symmetry of the insulating phase, revealing an optically induced monoclinic metal. Only at substantially higher fluences does the symmetry fully recover to that of the high-temperature phase. These results demonstrate a nonequilibrium decoupling of metallicity and structural symmetry and establish simultaneous multiprobe spectroscopy as a powerful approach for identifying emergent phases in correlated materials.
summary: This experiment uses ultrafast spectroscopy on $	ext{NdNiO}_3$ to study its metal-insulator transition. By simultaneously measuring reflectivity and SHG, the researchers found that optical excitation can drive the material into a metastable state that is metallic but structurally retains the symmetry of the insulating phase. This proves a non-equilibrium decoupling between electronic metallicity and structural symmetry in correlated oxides.
main_problem: The study investigates whether electronic and structural order remain coupled when a correlated material undergoes a metal-insulator transition under non-equilibrium, photoinduced conditions.
main_result: The research demonstrates a non-equilibrium decoupling where optical excitation can stabilize a metastable state exhibiting metallic reflectivity while retaining the structural symmetry of the insulating phase.
method: The authors employed simultaneous time-resolved multi-probe spectroscopy, measuring linear optical reflectivity and symmetry-sensitive second-harmonic generation (SHG) on $	ext{NdNiO}_3$.
model_or_system: The physical system is $	ext{NdNiO}_3$, a correlated oxide known for a first-order metal-insulator transition between a high-temperature orthorhombic metal and a low-temperature monoclinic insulator. Measurements are performed on thin films.
key_observables: Time-resolved reflectivity ($\Delta R/R$) to track metallicity, and SHG intensity/polarization dependence to track structural symmetry (monoclinicity).
important_parameters: Excitation fluence (ranging from low to high), time delay (sub-picosecond to ps scale), and temperature (near the phase transition point).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that changes in reflectivity and SHG are direct, measurable indicators of the electronic and structural order parameters, respectively.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate static measurements confirming the equilibrium phase transition and symmetry, and time-resolved traces showing the rapid change in reflectivity versus the more gradual change in symmetry following optical excitation.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the equilibrium phase diagram using static measurements. It then uses time-resolved spectroscopy to probe the non-equilibrium dynamics, comparing the fluence dependence of the metallic signal versus the symmetry recovery to identify the transient, decoupled state.
why_interesting: The observation of transient, decoupled electronic and structural states provides a powerful experimental platform for studying non-equilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems, which is relevant to understanding quench dynamics in quantum materials.
